messages:
Samir: Heads up — noticed p99 TTFT on the token-level SLO dashboard jumped in us-west this morning, but tokens/sec is low for those traces so I think sampling is masking the real distribution. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/tiles/zk12
Liz: Can you paste the panel query? Thinking sampling rate + histogram buckets might be wrong.
Samir: Sure. Current panel uses a recording rule and a histogram_quantile over a prometheus_histogram_metric we derive from token latencies. Query:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region))
```
But we aggregate across customers and then sample at scrape time with a scrape_scrubber that drops 80% of low-cardinality labels.
Oscar: That scrubber saves TSDB cost but will bias high-percentiles when heavy-tailed requests are sub-sampled. If a few large tail requests are kept but many mid tail are dropped, p99 looks worse or better depending on which hits land.
Mira: Correct — we saw this before on embedder shards. Options: lower sampling for token latency buckets, move to exemplar sampling, or compute p99 in the app and export as a gauge per model-shard.
Kevin: App-side p99 per-shard sounds accurate but increases custom metrics and cardinality. How bad is the cost impact?
Samir: Quick numbers: sampling=20% saved ~60% cardinality last quarter. App-side gauges would add ~0.25M series if we do per-model-per-shard-per-region, roughly +12% to TSDB.
Liz: Proposal: Add a dedicated panel that slices p50/p95/p99 by sample-presence label (sampled=1/0) so we can see bias, and change the alert to fire only when p99(sampled=1) and tokens/sec>threshold. That avoids noise from tiny-volume tails.
Oscar: I like that. Also tune alert to use increase(tokens_count[5m]) > 500 to avoid noisy pages for low traffic models.
Mira: Implementation notes — two parts: 1) recording rule change to keep an unsampled histogram series for heavy models (label allowlist), 2) panel update to show sampled vs unsampled, and 3) alert rule add tokens/sec gating. Example recording rule tweak:
```yaml
- record: token_latency_seconds_bucket_unsampled
  expr: token_latency_seconds_bucket
  labels:
    sampled: "0"
  for: 0s
```
(we'd only apply via relabeling to targets in allowlist)
Kevin: Are we ok with maintaining allowlist? Operations burden vs cost tradeoff. Maybe auto-allowlist top N models by qps.
Samir: We can auto-generate allowlist from the top-100 tokens/sec weekly job. Low manual ops.
Liz: For the Grafana panel, use join on labels so users can toggle sampled vs unsampled. Also add tokens/sec heatmap below so people can correlate ttft spikes with workload density.
opsbot: deploy-grafana: dashboard patch queued (#4321) by Samir — runtime/ttft-sampling-panel update.
grafana-bot: patch preview: https://grafana.redwood/d/preview/ttft-sampling-surgery
Oscar: After deploy, let's run a backtest over last 72h to compare alerts with and without token gating. I can script a replay against prometheus data.
Samir: I'll own the recording rule PR and the allowlist generator. Liz can own the panel layout and alert rewrite. Oscar will run the backtest. Mira and Kevin to review cost estimates.
Liz: Quick note on queries — prefer using increase(tokens_total[5m]) instead of rate() in alerting to avoid scrape-window edge cases.
Samir: Agreed. Example alert condition:
```
- alert: TokenTTFT_P99_Exceeded
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(increase(token_latency_seconds_bucket_unsampled[5m])) by (le, model, region)) > 0.5
  for: 5m
  annotations:
    runbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/runbooks/ttft_p99
  labels:
    severity: page
```
Kevin: LGTM pending cost review. Also add note to rollout: canary to us-west only for 24h then global.
Samir: Will do canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Liz: Filed follow-ups: GH#778 (recording rule), GH#779 (dashboard), GH#780 (backtest).
Mira: Adding retention/cost calc to GH#778 discussion.
Samir: Closing the thread — will update when canary goes green.
